Core principle: Business architecture is about the business.
Meaning in plain words: Describe capabilities, value and information in business terms; do not start from systems.
column6: 10 and 14 are written in business language; technology comes later.

Core principle: Business architecture's scope is the scope of the business.
Meaning in plain words: Include the whole ecosystem, with customers, partners and outsourced capabilities, not just internal units.
How this template applies it: Stakeholders and value stream cover external parties.

Meaning in plain words: The guide gives a framework to adapt, not a fixed method or tool.
How this template applies it: The template is configurable; add or drop registers.

Meaning in plain words: Build in passes and refine; do not wait for completeness.
How this template applies it: Versioned registers, definition of done, gates.

Meaning in plain words: Content built once serves many scenarios and initiatives.
How this template applies it: One knowledgebase feeds document, deck and workbook.

Core principle: Business architecture is not about the deliverables.
Meaning in plain words: The value is shared understanding and better decisions, not the diagrams themselves.
How this template applies it: Gates test whether decisions were made, not only whether artefacts exist.
